papers.title: From Genes to Neural Circuits: Genetic and Systems Mechanisms of Ethanol Sensitivity and Tolerance in Drosophila melanogaster.
papers.abstract: Alcohol use disorder (AUD) is a complex neuropsychiatric disease shaped by genetic, environmental, and physiological factors. Over four decades, Drosophila melanogaster has emerged as a powerful model for dissecting the molecular and neural mechanisms underlying ethanol sensitivity, tolerance, preference, and consumption. Its conserved signaling pathways, sophisticated genetic toolkit, and robust behavioral assays have enabled discovery of genes and neural circuits governing alcohol responses across biological levels. This review summarizes major advances in the genetics and neurobiology of ethanol-related behaviors in Drosophila. Forward genetic screens identified conserved regulators of ethanol sensitivity and tolerance, including cAMP/PKA signaling components, ion channels, neurotransmitter receptors, cytoskeletal regulators, and neuropeptide pathways. Subsequent studies revealed distinct roles for the ellipsoid body, mushroom bodies, circadian neurons, and barrier glia in intoxication, tolerance, and reward. Epigenetic studies further established chromatin remodeling and transcriptional regulation as mechanisms of long-term behavioral plasticity, while systems genetics and genome-wide association studies highlighted the polygenic basis of natural variation in alcohol-related traits. Together, these findings advance an integrated view of ethanol action and provide a framework for understanding human AUD. Emerging approaches include single-cell and connectomics analyses, functional testing of human variants, and integration of systems genetics with circuit neuroscience.

papers.title: Progress in research on the bidirectional relationship between circadian rhythm and depression: A bibliometric analysis.
papers.abstract: This study used VOSviewer and CiteSpace to conduct a bibliometric analysis of 444 publications on the relationship between circadian rhythms and depression, retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection (January 2015 to April 2025). Publication numbers remained low until 2017 but increased markedly after 2018, with the United States contributing the largest share. Ian B. Hickie and Joanne S. Carpenter were the most prolific authors; the University of Pittsburgh and Chronobiology International were the most productive institution and journal, respectively. McClung, Dubocovich, and Logan were the top co-cited authors, while frequent keywords included "expression," "sleep," "circadian rhythms," and "melatonin." These findings underscore the growing importance of circadian rhythms in depression pathophysiology and therapy, with future research likely to focus on diagnosis, biomarker identification, individualized treatment, prognosis, and health management.

papers.title: Additive Effects of Time Awake and Number of Flights on Fatigue in Short-Haul Pilots: Implications for Duty Time Regulation.
papers.abstract: Time awake affects airline pilots' fatigue but it is less clear how workload during that time awake impacts fatigue. Although current flight time limitations take the number of flights within a duty period as a measure of workload into account, quantitative evidence for its fatiguing effect is scarce. Here, we analysed fatigue, subjective workload and flight-associated hassles at the end of 553 short-haul flights from 37 airline pilots. Two linear mixed-models with fatigue or subjective workload as the dependent variable were generated, adjusted for time awake, number of completed flights, number of hassles, prior sleep and pilot's responsibility (flying/monitoring). Results showed that fatigue was influenced by time awake, number of flights and pilot's responsibility, whereas no effect was found for number of hassles. The critical fatigue threshold (flying not recommended) was exceeded 2.4 h earlier when operating four flights compared with one flight. Fatigue was lower but subjective workload was higher when the pilot was flying instead of monitoring. Subjective workload increased with number of hassles, but not with number of flights or time awake. European duty time limitations are justified to include a penalty for additional flights but may underestimate the fatiguing effect.

papers.title: Sleep, inflammation, and pain in musculoskeletal rehabilitation: a structured integrative review of neurobiological mechanisms and non-pharmacological pain management strategies.
papers.abstract: Sleep disturbance, inflammation, and persistent pain may reinforce one another, compromising musculoskeletal rehabilitation. To synthesize evidence on mechanisms linking sleep, inflammation, and pain and identify relevant non-pharmacological interventions. This structured integrative review examined peer-reviewed studies published from January 2010 to December 2025, identified through PubMed, Scopus, PEDro, and SciELO. Reporting and synthesis were guided by SANRA and EQUATOR recommendations. Fifty-seven studies were included: 24 experimental or observational studies, 17 systematic reviews or meta-analyses, and 16 narrative or integrative reviews. Sleep restriction was associated with changes in interleukin-6, tumor necrosis factor-α, and C-reactive protein, with responses varying across populations and protocols. Prostaglandins and bradykinin may promote nociceptive sensitization, while disrupted sleep may impair descending pain inhibition. Exercise, manual therapy, neuromuscular electrical stimulation, low-level laser therapy, and sleep-focused behavioral interventions showed mechanistic plausibility, although confirmatory trials remain limited. Sleep assessment and sleep-focused interventions should be considered within multimodal musculoskeletal pain management, while further controlled research clarifies clinical effectiveness.

papers.title: Beyond seasonality: Rethinking daylight exposure in adolescent sleep research.
The association of particulate matter 2.5 exposure with frailty trajectories in middle-aged and older Chinese adults and the potential modification by lifestyle and socioeconomic status.
papers.abstract: To examine PM2.5 exposure associations with frailty trajectories in middle-aged and older Chinese adults, and evaluate modifying effects of lifestyle and socioeconomic status (SES). We analyzed 10,659 participants from CHARLS using PM2.5 data from Dalhousie University. Frailty was assessed via a deficit accumulation index. Group-based trajectory modelling (GBTM) identified frailty trajectories; ordered logistic regression estimated associations and effect modifications. Three trajectories emerged: "Stable low" (63.95%), "Increased to frailty" (29.00%), and "Continuously worsening" (7.05%). Each 10 μg/m³ PM2.5 increase raised odds of Trajectories 2 and 3 by 15.2% and 12.3%, respectively. Higher SES attenuated PM2.5 effects (RERI=-0.067), while unhealthy sleep duration amplified them (RERI=0.163). PM2.5 exposure is associated with deteriorating frailty trajectories. Higher SES exerts an antagonistic effect, whereas unhealthy sleep duration has a synergistic effect on PM2.5-related frailty progression.
papers.journal: Journal of occupational and environmental medicine

papers.title: Relationship between objective sleep efficiency and psychological distress in middle-aged and older Japanese: Results by work in the Shika study.
papers.abstract: Sleep quality and work, as factors related to psychological distress, have not yet been elucidated. Additionally, few studies have examined the association between sleep efficiency and psychological distress, which may affect psychological distress in middle-aged and older adults according to their work status. This study aimed to examine and clarify the relationship between sleep efficiency and psychological distress in middle-aged and older Japanese stratified by work and sex. A cross-sectional study was performed among community dwellers aged 40-90 years living in Shika-machi, Ishikawa, Japan, between January 2018 and April 2020. Psychological distress was assessed utilizing the Kessler 6 scale (K6), a psychological distress scale. Sleep efficiency was measured using actigraphy (MTI-220, ACOS Co., Ltd., Nagano, Japan) that includes the sleep index, and analyses were stratified by work status and sex. A multiple logistic regression analysis was conducted setting the high K6 group as an objective variable. A total of 360 middle-aged and older adults (women = 54.4%; mean age = 63.09 ± 10.48 years) were included in this study. Psychological distress, adjusted for confounders, was associated with low sleep efficiency (β = -0.060, p = 0.013) only among working women. We found no evidence of a relationship between other indicators of psychological distress in men with or without work and women without work. These results reveal a relationship between psychological distress and sleep efficiency among middle-aged and older working women, suggesting that work and poor sleep efficiency may be associated with greater psychological distress. Future studies should examine the relationship between psychological distress and sleep efficiency in women middle-aged and older using longitudinal studies that consider work-related effects.

papers.title: Unilateral nonarteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy associated with obstructive sleep apnea-hypopnea syndrome: a case report.
papers.abstract: This report describes a case of obstructive sleep apnea-hypopnea syndrome (OSAHS) associated with nonarteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy (NAION). NAION is an optic neuropathy characterized by painless vision loss, visual field defects, and optic disc edema. It results from hypoperfusion of the short posterior ciliary arteries, leading to acute ischemia and structural and functional impairment of the optic nerve, which ultimately manifests as blurred vision or blindness. We report the case of a 59-year-old Han Chinese male who presented with a 6-day history of blurred vision and visual field defects in the left eye. The diagnosis was confirmed after excluding other potential etiologies. The patient was treated with 80 mg of oral methylprednisolone, which was gradually tapered, alongside neuroprotective and circulation-improving therapies. Following consultation with the Department of Respiratory and Sleep Medicine, he was initiated on noninvasive ventilation (NIV) to correct systemic hypoxia and received bronchodilators. Subsequently, the patient's symptoms showed moderate improvement. NAION is frequently associated with a variety of systemic vascular risk factors, particularly hypertension, diabetes mellitus, dyslipidemia, ischemic heart disease, and cerebrovascular disease. These conditions compromise the microvascular supply to the optic nerve head, leading to ischemia, necrosis, and subsequent optic atrophy. Among these, OSAHS is recognized as a significant and independent risk factor. OSAHS is a clinical syndrome characterized by recurrent episodes of apnea and hypopnea during sleep, resulting in intermittent hypoxia, hypercapnia, and sleep fragmentation. OSAHS is a well-established risk factor for systemic vascular comorbidities, including cardiovascular disease and diabetes mellitus. In the present case, an association between OSAHS and NAION was observed after excluding other potential confounding etiologies. These findings highlight the clinical importance of screening for and managing OSAHS in patients with NAION, providing a rationale for optimized therapeutic strategies.

papers.title: Association of insomnia with anxiety might be greater than that of depression among patients with gastrointestinal cancer: a network analysis.
papers.abstract: Patients with gastrointestinal cancer frequently encounter a myriad of sleep disorders, and these disturbances can profoundly exacerbate their psychological distress, particularly anxiety and depression. Elucidating the intricate relationship between sleep disorders and psychological disturbances holds paramount significance in enhancing the therapeutic efficacy and improving the survival outcomes for these patients. A cross-sectional study including 352 participants from two hospitals was conducted. Insomnia symptoms and psychological distress were assessed. Pearson correlation analysis and network analysis were used to determine the association between insomnia and psychological distress components. In this study, the prevalence of psychological distress was recorded at 45.2%, while the prevalence of difficulty initiating sleep (DIS), difficulty maintaining sleep (DMS), and early morning awakening (EMA) stood at 37.5%, 34.9%, and 46.9%, respectively. The partial correlation showed the strongest correlation was observed between DIS and anxiety, with a coefficient of 0.15 (0.00, 0.23), and no direct conditional association was observed between depression and any of the insomnia symptoms within the network analyzed. Emphasizing the crucial role of difficulty initiating sleep (DIS) in relation to anxiety deepens our understanding of the intricate interplay between physical and mental symptoms experienced by gastrointestinal cancer patients. By recognizing and comprehending these interconnected factors, healthcare professionals can devise more tailored therapeutic strategies, ultimately contributing to enhanced overall patient outcomes.

papers.title: Motor network neurophysiological (TMS-EEG) markers as predictors of outcomes of ventriculoperitoneal shunt sustained for over a year in normal pressure hydrocephalus.
papers.abstract: Current practice for normal pressure hydrocephalus (NPH) relies on clinical presentation, imaging, and various clinical procedures to determine the need for neurosurgical intervention, specifically the installation of a ventriculoperitoneal shunt (VPS). This study aimed to evaluate the utility of a TMS-evoked potential (TEP)-based assessment (Delphi-MD) for predicting sustained response (over one year) to VPS, serving as an ancillary test to the cerebrospinal fluid tap test (CTT). Forty-one patients with possible iNPH underwent Delphi-MD evaluation of wave form adherence (WFA), a composite measure assessing how closely their TEPs resembled an ideal benchmark TEP. Of these, 18 patients received VPS treatment following a multidisciplinary team decision based on standard practice, blinded to the TEP results. Response to the intervention was evaluated over a period of more than one year using the clinical global impression of change (CGIC) scale, in addition to assessments with a 10-meter timed up and go test and the modified Rankin scale. Responders had higher M1L WFA values at baseline (prior to VPS) than non-responders (median 0.51 [95% CI 0.36-0.76], median 0.14 [95% CI -0.02-0.38], respectively p = 0.012). M1L WFA was successful in distinguishing responders (11/18) from non-responders (7/18) with an ROC-AUC of 0.935 [bootstrap 95% CI 0.792-1.00], p < 0.0001. M1L WFA cutoff was established with LOOCV and produced 90.9% sensitivity, 85.7% specificity and 88.9% accuracy. In contrast the CTT result was unsuccessful in predicting shunt responsiveness. This study indicates that higher M1L WFA obtained through Delphi-MD (TMS-EEG), signifies better preservation and functional integrity of the motor network in patients with probable iNPH that had a sustained response to VPS than those that did not. Given replication of results in future independent cohorts, Delphi-MD shows promise as an objective, accurate, and accessible ancillary screening tool for iNPH candidates, prior to referral for VPS treatment. Registration number: MOH_2021-12-08_010449. Registration date: 11.09.2021. https://clinicaltrial.health.gov.il/clinicaltrials/?sort=experimentapproveddate_tdt+desc&page=1&searchQuery=MOH_2021-12-08_010449 .
papers.journal: Fluids and barriers of the CNS

papers.title: EEG-defined differences in functional networks following beta-band transcranial alternating current stimulation in patients with disorders of consciousness: a pilot study.
papers.abstract: Severe disruption of cortico-thalamocortical circuits underlies disorders of consciousness (DOC). Beta-band (20 Hz) transcranial alternating current stimulation (tACS) can be used to probe frontal oscillatory synchrony, yet its potential to acutely modulate large-scale network dynamics in DOC is unknown. We applied 20 Hz tACS (1 mA) for 30 min over the frontal cortex (F3 and F4, International 10-20 system) in 28 patients with DOC. Offline functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) was used to quantify hemoglobin (HbO)-based functional connectivity (FC) and graph-theoretical network properties, including small-world properties (clustering coefficient, Cp; path length, Lp) and global efficiency (global efficiency, Eg; local efficiency, Eloc) at pre-stimulation resting-state measurement for 5 min (pre-stim), the first post-stimulation resting-state measurement for 5 min (post-stim1), and the second post-stimulation resting-state measurement for 5 min (post-stim2). Subgroups were defined by baseline video-electroencephalography (vEEG) pathology as moderately abnormal (n = 11) and diffuse slowing (n = 14); 3 patients excluded (incomplete vEEG). Frontal 20 Hz tACS was associated with transient enhancement of FC across the measured cortical network at post-stim1 (pFDR < 0.05), selectively strengthening intra-and interhemispheric and intra-nodal connectivity before resolving by post-stim2. Crucially, the effects were pathology-dependent, and visual-motor integration pathways (right occipital lobe to left motor cortex; right primary somatosensory cortex to left occipital lobe) emerged exclusively in DOC patients with moderately abnormal background but not in those with diffuse slowing. Concurrent acute network reorganization at post-stim1 (all p < 0.05) featured increased Cp, Eg, and Eloc, along with decreased Lp, all normalizing by post-stim2. Clinically, Coma Recovery Scale-Revised scores correlated positively with average FC of HbO (pre-stim: r = 0.47; post-stim2: r = 0.41) and Area Under the Curve (AUC) of Eg (pre-stim: r = 0.44), and negatively with AUC of Lp (pre-stim: r = - 0.41; all p < 0.05). Frontal beta-tACS was associated with state-dependent changes in functional network organization in DOC, with dynamic fNIRS measures that may be useful for tracking these changes. These findings provide preliminary descriptive evidence of short-term network changes associated with beta-tACS and may help guide future controlled studies of targeted neuromodulation in patients with DOC.

papers.title: EEG microstate alterations in psychotic depression: prolonged microstate C duration and associations with psychotic symptoms.
papers.abstract: Major Depressive Disorder with psychotic features (MDD-Psy) represents a severe clinical subtype with distinct psychopathology, yet its underlying large-scale brain network dynamics, as measured by resting-state EEG microstates, remain poorly characterized. We compared 68 patients with MDD-Psy and 63 patients with MDD without psychotic features (MDD-NonPsy). Clinical assessment included the Kangduo Antidepressant Scale (KDAS) and the Brief Psychiatric Rating Scale (BPRS). Resting-state EEG microstate parameters (duration, time coverage, occurrence, and transition probabilities) were analyzed. Group comparisons employed Mann-Whitney U/t-tests with False Discovery Rate (FDR) correction. Correlations between microstate alterations and psychotic symptom severity were assessed using Spearman's rank correlation with FDR correction. The groups were comparable in age and sex. The MDD-Psy group exhibited significantly greater severity in thought disturbance, activation, and hostility (all p < 0.001). EEG microstate analysis revealed a significantly prolonged median duration of microstate C, putatively associated with salience-network-related activity in MDD-Psy (91.99 ms) versus MDD-NonPsy (85.56 ms; p-corr = 0.004). Altered transition probabilities characterized MDD-Psy, including increased B→A but decreased B→C and C→A transitions (all p-corr < 0.05). Furthermore, in the combined sample, the duration of microstate C positively correlated with thought disturbance (ρ = 0.243, p-FDR = 0.030), while the reduced B→C transition probability was strongly negatively correlated with both thought disturbance (ρ=-0.393, p-FDR < 0.001) and hostility. Within patients with major depressive disorder, the psychotic subtype is associated with a distinct pattern of aberrant resting-state brain network dynamics relative to the non-psychotic subtype, characterized by prolonged microstate C duration, commonly linked to salience network dynamics and reconfigured temporal transitions between the salience, visual, and auditory networks. The altered visual-to-salience network transition (B → C) demonstrated the most robust association with core psychotic symptom dimensions, including thought disturbance and hostility. These findings suggest that dysregulated dynamic coupling between perceptual processing and salience evaluation may represent a candidate neurophysiological indicator of psychotic features in depression. However, these results should be considered hypothesis-generating preliminary: the high rate of antipsychotic medication use in the MDD-Psy group, the absence of a healthy control group, and the cross-sectional design preclude tentative causal or specificity claims. Future longitudinal studies incorporating medication-naïve patients, healthy controls, and complementary neurophysiological markers are required to validate the clinical utility of these microstate alterations. Not applicable.

papers.title: The association between honey consumption amount and physical activity, sleep quality, and Nottingham health profile in young adults.
papers.abstract: Honey is a natural food with potential beneficial effects on health-related behaviors and well-being. However, evidence regarding the association between the amount of honey consumption and physical activity, sleep quality, and health-related quality of life in young adults remains limited. This study aimed to investigate the association between daily honey consumption and physical activity levels, sleep quality, and health-related quality of life among young adults. This cross-sectional comparative study was conducted in January 2026 among university students attending a public university in eastern Türkiye and residing in state dormitories. The required sample size was estimated as 336 through power analysis, and the study was completed with 468 participants. Participants were classified into five groups according to daily honey consumption level: non-consumers, 10, 20, 30, and 40 g per day. Data were collected using the International Physical Activity Questionnaire (IPAQ), the Richards-Campbell Sleep Questionnaire (RCSQ), and the Nottingham Health Profile (NHP). Data were analyzed using one-way ANOVA, correlation, and regression analyses. Most participants had a normal body mass index (BMI), and the mean age was comparable across groups. Among honey consumers, IPAQ scores were positively correlated with RCSQ scores (r = 0.27, p < 0.01), while significant negative correlations were found between IPAQ and NHP, and between RCSQ and NHP (r=-0.26 and r=-0.58, respectively; p < 0.01). Among non-consumers, the correlation between IPAQ and RCSQ was negative and non-significant (r=-0.03, p > 0.05), the correlation between IPAQ and NHP was positive and non-significant (r = 0.02, p > 0.05), and the correlation between RCSQ and NHP was significantly negative (r=-0.29, p < 0.01). Regression analyses indicated that honey consumption level was significantly associated with physical activity, accounting for 6.8% of the variance in IPAQ scores (F = 16.02, p < 0.01), with sleep quality, accounting for 6.4% of the variance in RCSQ scores (F = 31.60, p < 0.01), and with health-related quality of life, accounting for 8.2% of the variance in NHP scores (F = 19.68, p < 0.01). In young adults, daily honey consumption is associated with higher physical activity levels, better sleep quality, and a more favorable symptom burden as assessed by the NHP. Moreover, honey consumption level was significantly associated with variation in these health-related behaviors.

papers.title: Integrating task-state electroencephalography and motor function for intelligent assessment of recovery status from prolonged disorders of consciousness.
papers.abstract: Accurately assessing recovery in patients with prolonged disorders of consciousness (PDoC) is essential for evaluating the therapeutic efficacy and optimizing clinical care. However, substantial individual variability and poorly understood recovery mechanisms render this task exceptionally challenging. We collected task-state electroencephalography and clinical records from 78 PDoC patients to develop an intelligent assessment framework. Power spectral densities (PSDs) and coherence values (CVs) derived from event-related potentials (ERPs) were extracted and integrated with motor function scores to construct a multidimensional feature set. Linear support vector machine (SVM) and logistic regression (LR) models were built and rigorously evaluated via leave-one-out cross-validation (LOOCV). SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) was utilized for visual explanation. The LOOCV indicated that both LR and SVM achieved optimal, similar performance in integrating alpha-band features with motor function (Macro-Average F1-score [Ma-F]: 76.79% versus 75.54%). The Receiver Operating Characteristic curves (with Area Under the Curve values of 77.57% for LR and 72.82% for SVM) and Precision-Recall curves (with Average Precision values of 68.87% for LR and 59.85% for SVM) suggested that the framework performs stably. The reliability curves indicated that both models demonstrate good calibration and are reliable for assessment. The study provides preliminary evidence that alpha-band PSDs and CVs derived from ERPs potentially enhance the motor function assessment performance. This integrated paradigm provides a valuable indicator. Overall, our findings suggest that combining neuroscience with intelligent technology holds promise for improving personalized diagnosis and optimizing the PDoC management.

papers.title: Effect of aerobic and Pilates exercise on balance, gait, functional capacity, lower extremity strength, fear of falling, sleep quality, and quality of life in older adults.
papers.abstract: The primary objective was to compare the effects of aerobic and Pilates exercise programs on balance, gait performance, functional capacity, lower extremity strength, fear of falling, sleep quality, and quality of life in older adults. A secondary objective was to determine which exercise modality yields greater improvements in these outcomes, thereby providing evidence to guide the selection of effective exercise interventions for promoting health and well-being among the older adults. Forty-four older adults, aged 60-69 years, were randomly assigned into either the aerobic (n = 22) or Pilates exercise group (n = 22). The aerobic group trained three sessions per week (30 min of active exercise per session; 90 min/week), while the Pilates group (PG) trained two sessions per week (45 min of active exercise per session comprising mat, standing, and TheraBand components; 90 min/week), each for eight weeks, yielding equivalent total active exercise volumes (720 min per group). The outcomes of Mini-Balance Evaluation System Test (MBEST), Timed Up and Go test (TUGT), 2-Minute Walk Test (2MWT), 10-Meter Walk Test (10MWT), Five-Time Sit-to-Stand test (5xSTST) and self-reported questionnaires of the Fall Efficacy Scale International (FES-I), Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI), and WHOQOL-Brief were collected at baseline and post-treatment. Groups were equivalent at baseline across all measures. Significant Group × Time interaction effects were observed for gait velocity (10MWT) and dynamic balance (MBEST), with the aerobic group demonstrating significantly greater improvements in both (10MWT: p = 0.016; MBEST: p < 0.001). ANCOVA adjusting for baseline score, age, and BMI confirmed these between-group differences (10MWT: p = 0.012; MBEST: p < 0.001). Significant time main effects (p < 0.05) were observed for all remaining outcome measures (TUGT, 5×STST, 2MWT, FES-I, PSQI, all WHOQOL-Brief domains), indicating meaningful within-group improvements shared across both interventions. Both aerobic and Pilates exercise programs produced clinically meaningful improvements in gait velocity, functional capacity, and balance in older adults, with the aerobic group demonstrating significantly greater improvements in dynamic balance. Both interventions additionally reduced fall-risk classifications based on clinical threshold analyses. The findings of this study suggest that aerobic exercise may be the preferred modality for optimizing functional mobility and balance in community-dwelling older adults, though both modalities offer valuable and clinically meaningful health benefits. Future trials equalizing both volume and frequency are warranted to confirm modality-specific effects with full design equivalence. This Clinical Trial is registered with Thai Clinical Trials Registry (TCTR) approved by WHO. Registration number TCTR20240403002. Date of registration 13 March 2024. URL https//www.thaiclinicaltrials.org/#.

papers.title: Portable polysomnography-derived multi-domain EEG markers of anesthetic state transitions during propofol anesthesia for gastrointestinal endoscopy.
papers.abstract: Propofol anesthesia is widely used for gastrointestinal (GI) endoscopy, but electroencephalographic (EEG) features of anesthetic state transitions in this brief and stimulus-rich setting remain incompletely characterized. This study aimed to describe clinically interpretable EEG markers across anesthetic stages using portable polysomnography (PSG)-derived six-channel EEG. In this prospective observational study, 31 adults undergoing GI endoscopy under propofol-based anesthesia underwent continuous portable PSG recording. EEG analyses focused on six scalp channels (F3, F4, C3, C4, O1, and O2) across four clinically defined stages: baseline, induction, maintenance, and recovery. Relative spectral power, spectral edge frequency at 95% cumulative power (SEF95), and spindle-like event metrics were quantified. Sensor-level functional connectivity was assessed using weighted phase-lag index, imaginary coherence, and amplitude envelope correlation (AEC). Spectral and spindle-like event measures were analyzed using linear mixed-effects models, and connectivity differences were assessed using permutation-based paired tests with false discovery rate correction. Relative delta power decreased from baseline and induction to maintenance and recovery, whereas theta, alpha, sigma, and beta relative power and SEF95 generally increased. Spindle-like event density differed across stages and was highest during recovery, while mean duration and peak frequency remained relatively stable within the 11-16 Hz range. Functional connectivity showed metric-specific modulation: AEC demonstrated the most widespread stage-related differences, whereas phase-based connectivity measures showed only limited edge-specific changes after correction for multiple comparisons. Portable PSG-derived six-channel EEG captured stage-related spectral, spindle-like event, and sensor-level connectivity changes during propofol anesthesia for GI endoscopy. These findings identify candidate EEG features for future evaluation of emergence detection and atypical anesthetic-state identification during procedural anesthesia. Their utility for real-time propofol titration or excessive-sedation warning requires prospective validation.

papers.title: Theta-Band Temporal Interference Stimulation Modulates Food Reward Prediction Error Encoding in Individuals with Elevated Food Addiction Symptoms.
papers.abstract: Prediction error (PE) signals support feedback evaluation and adaptive updating, and are closely linked to medial frontal theta dynamics, particularly within dorsal anterior cingulate cortex (dACC)-centered networks. However, evidence linking these oscillatory mechanisms to the modulation of PE encoding remains limited. Here, we tested whether theta-band modulation of a dACC-centered medial frontal network altered trial-level PE encoding during food-reward processing. In a single-blind, sham-controlled pre-post design, individuals with elevated food addiction symptoms performed a food incentive-delay task while undergoing electroencephalographic recordings combined with theta-band temporal interference stimulation. Single-trial analyses revealed that feedback-related negativity (FRN) amplitudes varied as a function of both behavioral and model-derived prediction errors. Critically, theta-band modulation altered FRN-PE coupling, with the effect most pronounced for unfavorable outcomes, whereas anticipatory activity remained unchanged. These findings support the hypothesis that theta-band modulation can alter feedback-related PE encoding within this population and task context.
